What is Uizard?

AI-first UI prototyping tool aimed at non-designers. Generates multi-screen app and web prototypes from a text prompt, converts hand-drawn wireframe sketches or screenshots into editable designs, and extracts themes from any image. Acquired by Miro in 2024.

Best for

Non-designers producing a credible clickable prototype quickly.

Main features

  • Autodesigner generating multi-screen prototypes from a text prompt
  • Wireframe Scanner converting hand-drawn sketches into editable digital designs
  • Screenshot Scanner turning any app screenshot into an editable design
  • Theme Generator extracting a colour and font theme from an image or URL
  • drag-and-drop editor with component library
  • interactive prototype linking
  • Figma export
  • collaboration and commenting.

Practical use cases

  • Turning a whiteboard sketch of an app into a clickable prototype
  • producing a prototype for a stakeholder review in an hour
  • generating a design starting point that a real designer then refines in Figma
  • user-testing a concept before committing engineering time.

Who is it for?

  • Product managers, founders, developers, marketers and anyone who needs a prototype without design skills.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium per-seat subscription

Plans described in the source

Free $0 with 2 projects, limited AI generations (historically ~100 components per project) and Uizard watermarking. Pro around $19/creator/mo billed annually ($39 monthly) with unlimited projects, unlimited AI generations and no watermark. Business around $39/creator/mo annually with team features, custom fonts and priority support. Enterprise custom. Annual billing roughly 50% cheaper than monthly, which is an unusually large gap.

Free plan

Yes - free tier with 2 projects, watermarked, adequate for evaluation only.

Free trial

Yes - Pro trials offered; the free tier allows indefinite limited use.

Usage limits to consider

Free tier limits to 2 projects and caps components and AI generations, with watermarking. Autodesigner generations are limited on free. Viewer seats are typically unlimited; creator seats are charged.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • The Wireframe Scanner turning a paper sketch into an editable digital design is genuinely delightful and unmatched here
  • Autodesigner produces multi-screen prototypes fast enough to change how early product conversations happen
  • accessible to people with zero design training
  • Figma export means designers can take over cleanly.

Limitations to consider

  • Output quality is clearly below what a designer would produce - it is for validation, not delivery
  • component library is limited compared with Figma
  • the Miro acquisition raises questions about long-term standalone investment
  • monthly pricing is poor value versus annual
  • not suitable for design systems or production handoff.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web
  • Figma export
  • Miro integration since acquisition

Languages

  • English interface; designs can contain any language

API access

No public API

Integrations and exports

  • Figma export, Miro, Sketch import, PNG/PDF export

Evaluation notes

Use Uizard to get to a testable prototype, then move to Figma for anything that will ship - treating Uizard output as final design is where teams get into trouble. The sketch scanner is the feature most worth trialling.
